RandomX-in-the-browser is an *experiment*, not the VoltMiner product miner.

The Android app uses the bundled XMRig binary (MoneroOcean fork) speaking
TLS stratum to gulf.moneroocean.stream:20032 — RandomX native, DONATE 0%.

This folder is where a compiled WebRandomX (tevador/RandomX → Wasm) build
would live:

  web-randomx.js
  web-randomx.wasm

Those files are NOT committed. They are ~tens of MB of Emscripten output
(WebRandomX links with TOTAL_MEMORY=272MB). Build them yourself if you
want the tab to actually hash:

  git clone https://github.com/WebCryptomining/WebRandomX.git
  cd WebRandomX && mkdir build && cd build
  emcmake cmake -DARCH=native ..
  make
  cp web-randomx.js web-randomx.wasm  <this-dir>/

License of RandomX / WebRandomX is BSD-3-Clause (see that repo). Do not
hotlink a third-party wasm at runtime.

Without those two files, miner-worker.js still talks to the VPS bridge
and will receive rx/0 jobs, but it will not submit shares (no fake PoW).

The hop itself is tools/web-stratum-bridge (VPS / localhost), not a
Cloudflare Worker.
